rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes varying alloy composition and heat treatments to adjust lattice misfit, while the paper uses high-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering on a specific CoCrFeNiTi powder mixture. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (compositional tuning vs. mechanical alloying and sintering).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies room temperature and elevated temperature (673–1073 K) deformation tests, whereas the paper involves milling at 400 rpm, SPS at 900–1000°C, and room-temperature hardness/compression testing. The processing conditions are entirely different, and the testing temperature regimes only partially overlap.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes edge dislocation-mediated plasticity due to lattice distortions, while the paper attributes strengthening to grain boundary (Hall-Petch), dislocation density, and solid solution strengthening with a specific FCC/BCC phase mix. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased hardness and strength with a thermal strength plateau, while the paper reports a specific hardness of 675 Hv and compressive strength of 1894 MPa with intergranular fracture. The predicted property direction is similar (increased strength/hardness), but the specifics and underlying rationale differ.
